values.title: Product Wishlist
user_stories: As a shopper, I want to tap a heart button on a product card in the product list, so that I can save products I like without leaving the list.
As a shopper, I want a heart button on the product page, so that I can save or unsave a product while looking at its details.
As a shopper, I want a Wishlist page that lists my saved products, so that I can find them again later in the same browser session.
As a shopper, I want to remove a product from my wishlist, so that the list only holds products I still care about.
acceptance_criteria: Given a product that is not in my wishlist, When I click the heart button on its product card in the product list, Then the heart shows as filled (saved) and the product appears on the Wishlist page.
Given a product that is not in my wishlist, When I click the heart button on its product page, Then the heart shows as filled and the product appears on the Wishlist page.
Given a product that is in my wishlist, When I click its filled heart on a product card or product page, Then the heart shows as empty and the product no longer appears on the Wishlist page.
Given I have saved products, When I open the Wishlist page from a link in the site header, Then each saved product is listed with its name, image and price, and links to its product page.
Given my wishlist is empty, When I open the Wishlist page, Then I see a message saying my wishlist is empty and a link back to the products.
Given I saved a product, When I reload the page or navigate to another page, Then the product is still saved and its heart is still filled on the product list and product page.
Given two different browser sessions, When one session saves a product, Then the other session's wishlist does not contain it.
Given a product is already in my wishlist, When it is saved again (e.g. repeated click or request), Then it appears only once on the Wishlist page.
out_of_scope: User accounts or sharing a wishlist across devices or browsers.
Moving wishlist items into the cart (add-to-cart from the Wishlist page).
Wishlist item count badge in the header.
Price-drop or back-in-stock notifications for saved products.
Multiple or named wishlists, and sharing a wishlist via link.
Sorting or filtering the Wishlist page.

impact_analysis.summary: Add a wishlist stored on the server per X-Session-Id, built the same way as the cart: model + Alembic migration, a /api/wishlist router, a WishlistContext on the frontend, heart buttons on ProductCard and ProductDetail, a Wishlist page and a header link. Session scoping, keeping state across reloads and de-duplication all come from the existing cart patterns (session_id header, UniqueConstraint).
impact_analysis.db: New tables, e.g. wishlists (session_id unique, indexed, created_at) and wishlist_items (wishlist_id FK cascade, product_id FK, UniqueConstraint(wishlist_id, product_id)). Alternatively one table wishlist_items(session_id, product_id) with a unique constraint; the architect decides. Needs a new migration 0002 with down_revision='0001', and the model must be registered in api/models/__init__.py so conftest create_all and Alembic can see it. No seed changes.
impact_analysis.api: New api/routes/wishlist.py with prefix /api/wishlist (get, add, remove), using Depends(get_db) and Depends(get_session_id). Copy get_or_create_cart and to_cart_out from cart.py. Adding a product twice must be idempotent: no duplicate and no error. Unknown product returns 404, like the cart. Items need product_id, name, image and price_cents. New api/schemas/wishlist.py. Register the router in api/main.py. New api/tests/test_wishlist.py modelled on test_cart.py, including the separate-sessions test and an add-twice test.

The wishlist UI is built and every test passes: 16 unit tests and 5 end-to-end tests, including the 4 existing shop tests.

**What a shopper sees**
- **Header:** a new "Wishlist" link, placed between Products and Cart.
- **Product list:** each card has a heart in the top-right corner. Clicking it saves or unsaves the product without opening the product page, and the heart fills in when saved.
- **Product page:** the same heart sits next to "Add to cart".
- **Wishlist page:** lists each saved product with its image, its name (which links to the product page), its price and a Remove button. When the list is empty it says "Your wishlist is empty." with a "Browse products" link back to the list.

**Choices worth knowing about**
- **Double clicks:** while a save or unsave is still in progress, more clicks on that heart are ignored, so a fast double click doesn't save and then immediately unsave.
- **Duplicate saves:** a heart can only toggle, so a repeated click can't test this. The end-to-end test instead sends a second save request straight to the API, then checks the product appears only once on the Wishlist page.
- **Card structure:** the product card is now a box holding a link plus the heart button, rather than one big link, so the button isn't nested inside a link.
- **Test helper:** `renderPage()` now also wraps pages in the wishlist provider and includes a placeholder product page. The unit tests use it to check that clicking a card's heart doesn't open the product.

**Tests**
- **Unit tests:** a new `Wishlist.test.jsx` (empty state, listed items with links, removing). I added heart tests to `ProductList.test.jsx` and `ProductDetail.test.jsx`, and an empty-wishlist mock to the Cart and Checkout tests.
- **End-to-end:** `e2e/tests/wishlist.spec.js` is one test of the whole journey against the real API. It covers the empty state, opening the page from the header, saving from the list and from the product page, staying saved after a reload, that a second browser session doesn't see the items, and removing via the heart and via Remove.

review.summary: Clean, focused change that copies the existing cart patterns: get_or_create, to_*_out and the session dependency. All queries go through the SQLAlchemy ORM with no raw SQL. Every query is scoped to X-Session-Id, and tests show one session cannot see or change another's wishlist. The API, api.js and the tests match the contract, and every acceptance criterion is covered by API, Vitest or Playwright tests. I found a few minor robustness and polish points but no blockers.

findings.finding: The idempotent add is check-then-insert. If two POSTs for the same product arrive at the same moment, the second hits the UniqueConstraint and returns a 500 instead of 201. Catch IntegrityError, roll back and return the wishlist.
There is no loading state. The context starts as EMPTY_WISHLIST, so on a direct load of /wishlist a shopper with saved items briefly sees 'Your wishlist is empty.' until the GET returns.

No caller outside the provider uses 'refresh', yet the context still exposes it. The Promise.resolve().then(...) wrapper adds nothing over calling api.getWishlist() directly. Errors from toggle and remove are swallowed silently, so the shopper gets no feedback when one fails.

The contract lists 400 for a missing or invalid X-Session-Id, but get_session_id actually returns 422, and the test asserts 422. The contract defers to the existing behaviour, so this is fine, but the contract text should be corrected.
The card changed from a Link to a div wrapping a Link, so the heart button is no longer nested inside an anchor. This is a sensible fix for valid HTML and accessibility.

values.release_notes:
Corner Shop 1.1.0 (2026-10-18): Product Wishlist (REQ-001)

Shoppers can now save products they like. A heart button on each product card and on the product page saves or unsaves a product without leaving the page. A new Wishlist page, linked from the header, lists saved products in the order they were added, and shoppers can remove products from it. The wishlist lasts for the current browser session.

Technical: new API endpoints GET /api/wishlist, POST /api/wishlist (idempotent; 404 for an unknown product) and DELETE /api/wishlist/{product_id} (404 if the product is not in the wishlist). New tables wishlists and wishlist_items (Alembic migration 0002). Heart buttons ignore extra clicks while a save or unsave is in progress.

Testing: 27 API tests, 16 frontend unit tests and 5 e2e tests pass. Migration upgrade and downgrade were checked.
highlights: Heart button on product cards and the product page saves or unsaves a product
New Wishlist page linked from the header, with remove
New API endpoints: GET/POST /api/wishlist and DELETE /api/wishlist/{product_id}
